definition: S corporation account of undistributed taxable income earned in S years; distributions from it come out before accumulated E&P.
A lower standard than material participation (for example, approving tenants and setting rents) that allows up to $25,000 of rental real estate losses against other income.
A 0.9% tax on wages and self-employment income above $200,000 (single) or $250,000 (MFJ).
Corporations connected through a common parent owning at least 80% of vote and value; eligible to file a consolidated return.
Assigning nonbusiness income entirely to one state instead of apportioning it.
Dividing a multistate business's income among states using a formula of sales, property, and payroll factors.
The amount a taxpayer could actually lose: cash and property contributed plus recourse debt and qualified nonrecourse real estate financing.
The lifetime amount of taxable gifts and estate that the unified credit shelters ($13,990,000 for 2025).
A 21% corporate-level tax on an S corporation's gain from assets that had appreciated while it was a C corporation, if recognized within 5 years.
Regulations letting an eligible entity choose its federal tax classification on Form 8832.
A beneficiary's temporary right to withdraw a gift made to a trust, which turns the gift into a present interest eligible for the annual exclusion.
The ceiling on a trust's or estate's distribution deduction and on the amount beneficiaries are taxed on; it also determines the character of distributions.
A state's power to tax or require sales tax collection based on sales volume in the state, without physical presence.
A transaction in which an exempt organization gives a disqualified person more than it receives; subject to intermediate sanctions.
A trust whose income is taxed to the grantor because the grantor keeps certain powers or interests.
In an installment sale, gross profit divided by contract price; applied to each payment to find the gain recognized.
A payment to a partner for services or capital determined without regard to partnership income; deductible by the partnership and ordinary income to the partner.
Unrealized receivables (including depreciation recapture) and inventory; the partner's share produces ordinary income on the sale of a partnership interest.
A statutory stock option with no regular tax at exercise; a qualifying disposition produces long-term capital gain.
A transaction between members of a consolidated group; gain or loss is deferred until the item leaves the group.
MACRS convention required when more than 40% of a year's personal property is placed in service in the last quarter.
A 3.8% tax on the lesser of net investment income or MAGI above the threshold.
An option that produces ordinary income at exercise equal to the spread between FMV and the strike price.
Federal law barring state net income taxes on businesses whose only in-state activity is soliciting orders for tangible personal property.
A closely held corporation with mostly passive income; its undistributed income is subject to a 20% penalty tax.
A direct transfer from an IRA of an owner age 70½+ to charity; excluded from income and counts toward the RMD.
The Form 1120 (and 1065, 1120-S) schedule reconciling book income to taxable income.
Depreciable and real property used in a business and held more than 1 year; net gains are capital, net losses ordinary.
Small business stock whose losses are ordinary up to $50,000 ($100,000 MFJ) a year.
Nonrecognition for transfers of property to a corporation controlled (80%) by the transferors immediately after.
A partnership election to adjust the inside basis of its assets when an interest is sold or property is distributed.
An election to include restricted property in income at transfer rather than at vesting.
The test a special partnership allocation must meet to be respected under §704(b).
A state rule adding sales shipped to a state that can't tax the seller back into the origin state's sales factor.
The portion of an individual's gain on depreciable real property attributable to straight-line depreciation; taxed at up to 25%.
Income of an exempt organization from a regularly carried-on trade or business not substantially related to its exempt purpose.
